## YouTube and Reddit

YouTube. The lever is underrated. Its correlation with visibility is of the same order on ChatGPT, AI Mode and AI Overviews. 🟢 A Surfer SEO analysis (2025) of 46 million citations puts YouTube at the top of AI Overview sources, with 23.3% of citations. 🟡 In practice: explicit titles, chapters, clean transcripts, and a presence in other people’s videos.

Reddit. Its August 2026 drop concerns ChatGPT Search, not AI as a whole. It isn’t the first: in September 2025, the share of ChatGPT answers citing Reddit went from a peak of more than 14% to around 2% within a few weeks. One analyst attributed that episode to Google removing the num=100 parameter, rather than to a decision by OpenAI. 🟡 Reddit is still present in 83.9% of Google’s “Discussions and forums” blocks (Ahrefs, August 2026). 🟢

Conclusion: don’t build a ChatGPT strategy on Reddit, and don’t abandon it for Google. And if you go there, follow the rule I gave in the Barnacle article: roughly 90% useful contributions for 10% brand mentions. 🔵

## One cornerstone piece, repurposed everywhere

Whales, YouTube, forums, press: the list is daunting. Nobody can keep all these channels going by starting from scratch for each one. I start from a single cornerstone piece: solid expert content that answers a real question, with proof and, if possible, a piece of in-house data. Then I repurpose it.

1. A page on the website. This is the reference version, dated and structured, the one everything else points back to.

1. A long-form LinkedIn article. Signed by the expert, rewritten for that audience, with a link to the page.

1. Useful answers in forums. An answer to the question asked, not a summary of the article. The house rules and the 90/10 rule apply, and the August 2026 drop is a reminder not to bet everything on Reddit.

1. A short video. An explicit title, chapters, a clean transcript: that is what makes it readable for AIs.

1. A story for the press. A piece of data or a fresh angle interests a journalist. And it is press articles that may, later on, justify a line in an encyclopedic source, according to its own notability criteria.

![原文配图](../../../90_附件/GEO周收集_20261029_20261104/2116702945920123182/image-21.jpg)

This is not manufacturing consensus: each format brings real value to its audience, under your name. Each version repeats the same positioning statement and points back to the reference page.

The same reasoning applies to what the company already produces. A webinar, a conference talk, an interview, a campaign: their lifespan is counted in weeks. Turned into a page on the website, then broken down into answers and excerpts, they can become citable sources for months. 🔵 Before commissioning new content, take stock of what is lying dormant.

Ethics and risks

- Sponsored content. Label it as such. In France, undisclosed advertising counts as a misleading commercial practice, and the reputational risk is real.

- Barnacle, not parasite. Attaching yourself to a whale means bringing it real value: an expert answer, a tutorial, a deserved place in a comparison. Renting a subdirectory on an authoritative site to publish content without value there is parasite SEO. Since May 2024, Google has enforced its site reputation abuse policy through manual actions: the coupon and betting directories hosted by CNN, USA Today, Fortune or Outlook India were deindexed overnight. 🟢

- Manufacturing consensus. Since models end up treating as true what enough third parties repeat, there is a temptation to multiply the sources yourself. Citations are unstable, filters are improving, and a manufactured description becomes your reputation on the day it is exposed. 🔵

## 8. Measuring without kidding yourself

## Why a screenshot proves nothing

The same question never gives the same answer twice. Everything makes it vary: the model version, the mode (fast or thinking), the language, the location, the account’s memory, the moment. In the Ahrefs experiment, a cited page was on average only cited one eligible day in three. When someone claims to have tripled their visibility in a week, ask just one question: over how many runs, and with what variance?

The rule: sample. Each prompt is run several times, over several days, with the same procedure, each run in a new conversation. Note the date, the assistant, the mode and the model version when it is displayed. Compare rates, not anecdotes.

I measured this effect in a sector I know. I tracked 28 questions on accounting for freelancers in the Ahrefs Brand Radar prompt database (France), from July to October 2026, on ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, Perplexity and AI Overviews. From one monthly reading to the next, 72% of the brands named were still there. Only 31% of the cited URLs were still cited. ChatGPT renews its sources the most: it keeps only 16% of its URLs. On ChatGPT and Copilot, barely 6% of the URLs cited in July were still cited in August, September and October. “Best X” questions are the least stable, with 25% of URLs kept. 🟡

The limits, to be clear: Ahrefs re-tests each question once a month on ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot and Perplexity (every few days on AI Overviews), and each reading is a single answer. So the study measures stability from one month to the next, not from one day to the next, and part of the turnover probably comes from the randomness of each answer. One sector, one country. The practical lesson still holds: a single citation proves nothing, either way. Measure over several readings before drawing conclusions, and track mentions first, because they move far less than sources.

## A first sounding

Before tooling up, a manual baseline is enough:

- The assistants: ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Perplexity, Copilot, and Google’s AI Mode if possible. The Indy case shows why you should test them all, and more than once: at the end of July, Gemini almost never cited the most cited brand in its sector, then cited it more than 100 times per daily reading from the end of August (section 3).

- The conditions: a temporary chat, or a logged-out session. Private browsing isn’t enough if you stay logged in: the account’s memory and preferences follow you.

- The prompts: three phrasings of the same need, from three angles: a situation, a price, a material. For the roofer, by way of illustration: “my roof’s been leaking since the storm, I’m in Clifton, can someone come and tarp it tomorrow?”, “cheap roofer in Bedminster”, “who repairs slate roofs in Bristol?”.

- The record: mentioned or not, at what rank, with what argument, and which sources are listed.

If you are named on none of the variants, you are absent from the consideration phase for that need. This test is a thermometer, not a measurement.

When a competitor gets cited and you don’t, open the page it gets cited for and put it next to yours. Is the question in the title? Is the answer given up front? Are the figures dated and sourced? The gap often shows up there before it’s a matter of authority. 🔵

## Building your prompt set

No tool provides a reliable search volume for prompts: they are long, conversational, almost all unique. Think in intents. Good news: across 37,804 answers, Peec observes that highly crafted prompts and casual questions often bring up the same brands. 🟡 Intent matters more than wording. The exception: on unbranded commercial queries, small variations in wording already change the brands cited.

1. Start from the intent families of your business, phrased the way your customers phrase them. For Vinaxe: the need (“which software should I choose to manage the cellar of a small wine estate?”), the comparison, the price, the integration. For the roofer: the emergency, the price, the material, the neighbourhood.

1. Add real-life situations, without naming your product. “I run 12 hectares in Saumur with a cellar door shop open in summer, how do I stop counting my bottles in Excel?”

1. Add orphan topics: the concrete questions in your sector that nobody is defending yet (section 6). Also collect real phrasings: long queries from Search Console, questions asked to support or in reviews, and the “grounding queries” in Bing Webmaster Tools, that is, grouped phrasings of the searches run before citing you, across Copilot, Bing and partner integrations (not users’ exact prompts).

1. Add a handful of branded prompts: “X reviews”, “alternatives to X”, “X or Y”. In the United States, AI Overviews now appear on most branded searches (section 2): what is said about you there can be worked on.

1. Group by intent family, so you can read the results by theme.

1. Write in the language of the target market. A prompt in English tests the English-language web; a prompt in French tests the French web.

Also look at what assistants actually search for. Brand Radar’s AI Responses report shows, for ChatGPT and Perplexity, the fan-out queries generated from a prompt. 🟢 Don’t chase their volume: according to Ahrefs, more than 95% of these queries have no recurring search volume (March 2026). 🟡 What matters is the angles they reveal, not the exact words.

How many prompts? The right number follows from your capacity to record results, not from a universal rule. Each prompt must be run several times, on each assistant tracked. With three runs on four assistants, each prompt costs twelve answers to record per wave: 25 prompts already make 300. Start with what you can record every week without cheating, then expand once the routine is running smoothly.

To follow the same questions every week without copying answers by hand, Ahrefs Brand Radar offers custom prompts: your own prompts, tracked daily, weekly or monthly on AI Overviews, AI Mode, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Copilot and Claude. One check is one prompt on one assistant in one location, and each check is a single answer: read the rates over several weeks. 🟢

## Tracking AI traffic

- Analytics. Since 13 May 2026, GA4 has automatically classified traffic from the main assistants into a native “AI Assistant” channel, with no configuration. 🟢 Google gives ChatGPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, Copilot and Grok as examples, without publishing the full list. Perplexity is not named: check in your reports whether it lands in that channel or stays in “Referral”. So keep a custom channel group running in parallel, with the regular expression below as a “Source partially matches regex” condition, placed above “Referral”: below it, it captures nothing. ChatGPT also adds utm_source=chatgpt.com to many of its links. 🟡

- AI Overviews and AI Mode. In Analytics, their traffic is still counted as Google organic. Search Console, however, offers a “Generative AI performance” report, announced on 3 June 2026 and opened to all websites on 31 August 2026: impressions by page, country, device and date, but neither clicks nor queries. 🟢 To find out which queries are involved, filter the keywords that trigger an AI Overview in your SEO tool.

- Ahrefs Web Analytics. Ahrefs’ audience analytics tool isolates traffic coming from AI assistants (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini…) and shows which ones send you visits. 🟢

- Self-reported attribution. Add a “How did you hear about us?” question to your sign-up or quote forms, with AI assistants among the options. It captures what clicks miss: at Ahrefs, ChatGPT and Claude together account for 21.7% of sign-ups, based on what new customers report (October 2026). 🟡To turn these answers into revenue, see “Putting a number on the return”, further down in this section. 

- Copilot. The AI Performance report in Bing Webmaster Tools counts your citations in Copilot, in Bing’s AI summaries and in some partner integrations, without separating them, page by page, with grouped grounding queries (not users’ exact prompts). 🟢

- Server logs. AI crawlers don’t run your analytics script: they don’t show up as visits. Only the logs, or a bot analytics tool, reveal them. 🟢

- AI crawlers. A bot analytics tool plugged into your CDN or host (Cloudflare, Vercel, CloudFront, Fastly) sorts bot visits by category, including AI search, without touching your site’s code. Ahrefs’ Bot Analytics is one example. 🟢

- Direct traffic. Some visits from assistants arrive with no referrer, from an app or a copied link, and end up as “direct”. A rise in direct traffic to deep pages that nobody types in by hand is a clue worth checking against your records. 🔵

- Homepage. Since May 2026, most ChatGPT clicks land there. Don’t just measure your content pages.

(chatgpt\.com|openai\.com|perplexity\.ai|gemini\.google\.com|copilot\.microsoft\.com|claude\.ai|chat\.mistral\.ai|deepseek\.com|grok\.com)

With “partially matches regex”, the expression also captures subdomains such as www.perplexity.ai or chat.deepseek.com. With “matches regex”, GA4 requires the whole value to match, and those subdomains slip through. The expression includes Mistral’s Le Chat, not to be forgotten on the French market.

## Putting a number on the return

Leadership doesn’t fund a mention rate: it wants to know what GEO brings in. Part of what assistants do leaves no click and no referrer, so no figure will be exact. Aim for an honest estimate, always calculated the same way.

The calculation is the same as for any marketing investment: (gains attributed to GEO − GEO spend) ÷ GEO spend × 100.

On the spend side, split two families. Dedicated spend exists only for GEO: an assistant tracking tool, a specific engagement. Count it in full. Shared spend also serves SEO or content: writing, your SEO suite, team time. Keep only the share devoted to GEO, estimated with the people involved: an order of magnitude is enough.

On the gains side, cross two readings:

- What analytics sees. Conversions from the “AI Assistant” channel (or your custom group), multiplied by the average value of a customer. If your CRM passes real amounts, use those.

- What customers report. Among respondents to “How did you hear about us?”, work out the share that names an assistant, then apply that share to all new customers for the period. This reading also counts customers who met the brand through an assistant without ever clicking from it.

Fictional example, in round numbers, to illustrate the calculation: over a quarter, a dental practice in Austin, Texas pays $1,500 for a tracking tool and $9,000 for content, half of which serves GEO, so $6,000 of GEO spend. Analytics records 10 first appointments coming from assistants; a new patient is worth $700 on average over the first year, so $7,000 and a 17% return. On the survey side, 8 respondents out of 100 name an AI: applied to the quarter’s 200 new patients, that 8% gives 16 patients, so $11,200 and an 87% return. 🔵

A gap between the two readings is normal: show them side by side, and state that both fall short of the real effect. Run the same calculation every quarter, on periods after your market’s AI Overviews launch date (next subsection): the trend is what you read, not the single figure.

Measurement is already improving: ChatGPT often adds utm_source=chatgpt.com to its links, and Bing’s AI Performance report counts your pages’ citations in Copilot. Ads arriving in assistants will make paid clicks trackable and will probably push platforms to give advertisers more data, some of which may help organic measurement; nothing guarantees, though, that unpaid visibility will ever be measured as well as paid, so the self-reported reading keeps its value. Direct traffic, for its part, probably includes some AI (mobile apps, copied links, a brand name typed after reading an answer), but also bookmarks, emails, QR codes, messaging apps and returning visitors. A rise in direct traffic to deep pages (articles, guides), with no campaign or awareness effect to explain it and alongside rising AI visibility, is a signal to check against the survey, not proof (see “Direct traffic” above). 🟡

## A new baseline date

In France, 22 July 2026 cuts your curves in two. AI Overviews and AI Mode arrived that day, and the CTR of exposed domains fell straight afterwards (section 2). Comparing October 2026 with October 2025 therefore mixes two worlds. A drop in clicks may come from the AI Overview, not from your work. A rise may hide a decline relative to the rest of the market.

The rule: start again from a new baseline, from the end of July 2026, and compare later periods with each other, on the same pages and the same queries. Note the break date in your reports, so that nobody mistakes a mechanical drop for a failure. Search Console’s “Generative AI performance” report, open to all websites since 31 August 2026, lets you track the impressions of the pages concerned there. Outside France, use the launch date of the market you track.

## The tools

Several platforms track visibility in AI: Ahrefs Brand Radar, Semrush, Peec, Promptwatch, Profound, Similarweb, Otterly. Brand Radar, for example, separates cited pages from “found” pages. Your selection criteria:

- languages and countries covered, starting with the ones you sell in;

- assistants tracked;

- sampling frequency;

- export of full answers, not just scores.

Nothing obliges you to buy a tool before you start. A spreadsheet, your prompt set and a weekly record are enough to get going.

## 9. Special cases

## Health and sensitive topics (YMYL)

YMYL (Your Money or Your Life): that is Google’s term for topics that affect people’s health, money or safety. Health is the most exposed sector: 44.1% of medical queries trigger an AI Overview, more than double the average (Ahrefs, 146 million SERPs). 🟢 In France, it also comes top of the Ahrefs panel, at 22%, with CTR down 20% from the very first days. 🟢 An informational question with a short answer, and no transaction at the end, is exactly what the AI Overview absorbs.

ChatGPT’s targeting of specific domains, observed since August 2026, seems to favour sources that display expertise: institutions, specialist publishers. 🟡 For a practitioner’s website or a network of health sites:

- identified authors, credentials displayed, dated medical review;

- primary sources cited (learned societies, health authorities);

- complete About and legal notice pages;

- an up-to-date Google Business Profile listing, reviews, reference health directories, identical information everywhere;

- content an AI cannot provide: real fees, waiting times, care pathways, appointment booking.

## Local

Local searches rarely trigger an AI Overview: only 7.9% (Ahrefs, September 2025). 🟢 The battle is therefore mostly fought in conversational assistants, which rely on business listings, reviews, directories and the local press. 🟡

“Roofer in Bristol” remains a dead end. You need an area, a service and a situation: “emergency roof tarping after hail in Bedminster”. Keep an eye on the consistency of your name, address and phone number across all these sources.

## SaaS and products

For a software publisher like Vinaxe, two levers stand out from my case studies. The first is editorial: Indy answers its users’ practical questions better than anyone, and its most cited pages are guides, price scales and a comparison. The second is external: Lemlist’s presence in ChatGPT rests on G2, Capterra, Reddit and Trustpilot, fed by systematic review collection. On the website: public documentation, a clear pricing page, factual “alternatives” pages. And since a known brand’s new mentions mostly come from third parties (section 6), relationships with review sites, the trade press and video creators are part of GEO work.

## Starter checklist

- First sounding: three phrasings of the same need, in a temporary chat, on ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Perplexity and Copilot

- Source code without JavaScript, robots.txt and logs: OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, Googlebot and Bingbot allowed

- Indexing checked in Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools

- “Search generative AI” control checked in Search Console, decision documented, access to the property restricted

- Mirror test: “What do you know about [Brand]?”, sharp, vague or wrong portrait

- Prompt set sized to your recording capacity: intent families, real-life situations, orphan topics, a few branded prompts

- Baseline: each prompt run several times; mention, citation and recommendation rates; citation-to-mention ratio; share of voice

- Key prompts tracked over time, tagged by intent, in a spreadsheet or a tool such as Brand Radar custom prompts

- A single positioning statement, repeated on the website, LinkedIn and directories

- Key pages: one precise question per page, verifiable answer at the top, explicit structure, genuine update date

- 404s coming from assistants found and redirected to the right page

- Pages once cited or well ranked, now slipping, updated first

- About page, legal notice, directory listings, Google Business Profile

- Domains cited for your competitors mapped, three targets chosen, contribution plan per platform

- “AI Assistant” channel checked in GA4, custom channel group as a complement, crawler tracking in the logs

- “How did you hear about us?” question with an AI assistant option in your forms

- First return calculation: dedicated and shared spend, gains seen in analytics and gains reported by customers, repeated every quarter

- Search Console’s “Generative AI performance” report and Bing’s AI Performance report reviewed every month

- Homepage ready for a visitor arriving from an assistant

- New measurement after 4 to 6 weeks, compared with the baseline

## 11. Classic mistakes and myths

## The mistakes

- Confusing awareness with authority. Lots of mentions and few citations: that is Sage’s profile. Being known doesn’t make you a source.

- Cutting back editorial output because “SEO is dead”. At Indy, it is precisely the SEO content that feeds the AI citations.

- Waiting for ads in ChatGPT before taking an interest. Awareness can be bought, authority cannot.

- Confusing being present with being visible. A G2 profile with three reviews won’t lift you. In the Barnacle article, I put the critical mass at 50 to 200 reviews depen

- Turning up on Reddit with a sales pitch, or depending on a single domain: its share can collapse in a few days.

- Publishing pages in bulk without added value.

- Scattering mentions without context, which link the brand to no need at all.

- Leaving contradictory information on the About page, in directories and on business listings.

- Blocking GPTBot in the belief that you are leaving ChatGPT Search, or Google-Extended in the belief that you are leaving AI Overviews. For the latter, the lever is the Search Console control.

- Working on content while JavaScript makes the site unreadable for OpenAI’s, Anthropic’s and Perplexity’s crawlers.

- Steering by a screenshot or by a single run.

- Displaying a fake update date. Models read the content, not just the date.

- Forgetting the homepage, which now receives most ChatGPT clicks.
